exam.title: Design and Technology Paper 1 (17/1) - October/November 2021
exam.subject: Design and Technology
exam.description: Botswana Examinations Council, Junior Certificate Examination. Answer all 40 questions. Four possible answers are given for each; choose the one you think is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following should be worn to avoid respiratory hazards?
questions.explanation: Respiratory hazards are dust and fumes that are breathed in, so a dust mask (respirator), shown at C, must be worn. A is eye and face protection, B is gloves and D is safety boots.

questions.question: The diagram shows pieces of wood being glued together to make a joint. Which of the following is a requirement when applying glue as shown?
options: The glue that squeezes out of the bond line must be removed before drying.
The glue must be used in a closed room to avoid drying quickly and fumes.
The materials to be joined must be washed before glue is applied.
The materials to be joined must be clamped after glue dries.
questions.explanation: Excess glue that squeezes out of the joint should be wiped off while it is still wet; once dry it is hard to remove and stops finishes taking. Clamping is done while the glue is wet, and glue should be used in a well-ventilated room.

questions.question: The diagram shows a cup with a lid and a single-use straw. What type of structure is the cup?
questions.explanation: The cup is a thin outer skin wrapped around a hollow space, which is a shell structure.

questions.question: The diagram shows a cup with a lid and a single-use straw. Which of the following plastics is suitable to make the straw?
questions.explanation: Polypropylene is a flexible, food-safe thermoplastic that can be extruded into thin tubes and bent without cracking, which is why it is used for drinking straws. Acrylic is brittle and urea formaldehyde is a thermoset.

questions.question: Which of the following sockets is safe to use?
questions.explanation: In A a proper plug is pushed fully into an undamaged socket. B and C show broken sockets with the wiring exposed, and in D bare wires are pushed straight into the socket, all of which risk electric shock or fire.

questions.question: Which of the following is a mechanical property of adhesives?
questions.explanation: Mechanical properties describe how a material behaves under force, such as strength. Odour and colour are physical properties and flammability is a chemical property.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a safe practice of handling planes?
options: Choose the right plane for the task
Use fingers to clear off the shavings
Secure the work piece before planing
questions.explanation: Clearing shavings with your fingers can cut them on the blade. Shavings should be cleared with a piece of wood or a brush.

questions.question: Which of the following is a physical property of metals?
questions.explanation: Lustre (shine) is a physical property: it describes how a metal looks, not how it reacts to force. Brittleness, ductility and malleability are mechanical properties.

questions.question: Which of the following is a likely cause of structural failure?
questions.explanation: Poorly made joints and members weaken a structure and make it fail. Triangulation strengthens a structure, and an adequate load is one it is designed to carry.

questions.question: The diagram shows a method of holding a file. The diagram shows an appropriate grip for
questions.explanation: One hand holds the handle while the other presses down on the tip with the palm, putting weight on the file to remove material quickly. That is the grip for heavy filing; light filing uses only the fingertips on the tip.

questions.question: The diagram shows a method of deforming plastic. What is the name of the method illustrated on the diagram?
questions.explanation: A strip heater softens the plastic along a single line so the sheet can be bent along it. This is line bending.

questions.question: The diagram shows a method of deforming plastic. Plastics which are deformed using the above method have
questions.explanation: Line bending uses thermoplastics such as acrylic. They have plastic memory: when reheated, a bent piece returns to its original flat shape.

questions.question: The diagram shows a piece of wood with waste marked for removal. Which of the following planes can be used to remove the waste?
questions.explanation: The waste is a step along the edge of the wood, which is a rebate, so a rebate plane is used. A plough plane cuts grooves, and smoothing and jack planes flatten whole surfaces.

questions.question: The diagram shows a method of disposing waste. Which of the following statements is an advantage of the method?
options: Sorting various recyclable materials is difficult.
Quantity of materials to be handled increases.
Bio-degradable materials are difficult to manage.
Efficiency of collection and disposal of waste improves.
questions.explanation: Separating waste into paper, glass, plastic and metal bins at the source makes collection and recycling quicker and more efficient. The other options are disadvantages.

questions.question: The diagram shows an electrical component (a light bulb). Which of the following statements is true about the component?
options: Electrical current passes through the gas.
Electrical current passes through a vacuum.
Electrical current passes through a filament wire.
Electrical current causes electrons within to move and glow.
questions.explanation: In a filament lamp the current flows through a thin tungsten filament, which heats up until it glows. The gas only stops the filament burning out.

questions.question: The diagram shows an electrical component (a light bulb). Which of the following is the electronic symbol of the component?
questions.explanation: A lamp is drawn as a circle with a cross inside, shown at B. A is a phototransistor, C a light-emitting diode and D a buzzer.

questions.question: Which method of enhancing techniques was used on the diagram below?
questions.explanation: The wooden handle has been drawn with grain lines so it looks like real wood. Showing what a surface is made of in this way is texturing.

questions.question: What is the name of the fitting shown below?
questions.explanation: The plastic block screwed into the corner joins a side panel to the top. It is a modesty block, a knock-down fitting used in flat-pack furniture.

questions.question: The illustration shows a mechanism. What is the name of the mechanism shown?
questions.explanation: A toothed wheel with a catch (S) resting against its teeth is a ratchet and pawl.

questions.question: The illustration shows a mechanism. Which of the following is an advantage of the part labelled S?
options: Locks the teeth in one direction
It reduces the speed of rotation
questions.explanation: S is the pawl. It lets the wheel turn one way but drops between the teeth to stop it turning back.

questions.question: Which drawing technique has been used to present the design below?
questions.explanation: The vertical edges are upright and the horizontal edges run back at 30° on both sides, so the chair is drawn in isometric. The faint box around it is the crate used to construct the drawing.

questions.question: The diagram shows an electronic component (a push button). Which of the following is the symbol of the electronic component shown?
questions.explanation: The component is a push-to-make switch. Its symbol, at D, shows a bar that is pressed down onto two contacts. A is a double-pole switch, B a reed switch and C a two-way switch.

questions.question: Which of the following structures will result in instability and large deformation?
questions.explanation: A roof truss is stable when it is fully triangulated. In B the long members cross to form four-sided shapes that are not braced by triangles, so the truss can distort under load. A, C and D are made entirely of triangles.

questions.question: The diagram shows a piece of timber. Its thickness is 38 mm to 100 mm and its width is 150 mm or over; the length is standard. What is the commercial name of the timber shown?
questions.explanation: Sawn timber that is thick (about 38 to 100 mm) and wide (150 mm or more) is sold as a plank. Boards are thinner, and battens and strips are narrow.

questions.question: Which of the following are good characteristics of a flux?
options: Low melting temperature, facilitates wetting, and melts the base metals
High melting temperature, facilitates wetting, and melts the base metals
Low melting temperature, facilitates wetting, and protects a joint from oxidising
High melting temperature, facilitates wetting, and protects a joint from oxidising
questions.explanation: A flux melts at a low temperature, helps the solder flow over and wet the joint, and keeps air off the hot metal so it does not oxidise. A flux never melts the base metals.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about finishes and solvents?
options: Thinners is used for cleaning oil-based paint brushes.
Water is used for cleaning oil-based paint brushes.
Mineral spirit is used for thinning oil-based paint.
Turpentine is used only with water-based paints.
questions.explanation: Oil-based paint does not dissolve in water, so brushes are cleaned with thinners (or turpentine). Turpentine is a solvent for oil-based paints, not water-based ones.

questions.question: The diagram shows a man climbing a cliff. What type of forces are exerted on the rope as the man climbs the cliff?
questions.explanation: The climber's weight pulls the rope tight, which is tension, and as he turns on the rope it is twisted, which is torsion. A rope cannot carry compression because it simply goes slack.

questions.question: Which of the following illustrates a check?
questions.explanation: A check is a split that runs along the grain, usually caused by the surface drying faster than the inside. A shows these splits. D is a twisted board.

questions.question: Which of the following bits is suitable to drill on bricks or concrete?
questions.explanation: A masonry bit, shown at C, has a wide tungsten carbide tip that is wider than the flutes behind it, so it can grind through brick and concrete. A and B are twist bits and D is an auger bit for wood.

questions.question: The term electrical resistance refers to
options: the amount of energy a bulb uses in a circuit.
the force of electricity within an electric circuit.
the reduction of current flow in an electric circuit.
the power which flows in one direction in a circuit.
questions.explanation: Resistance is how much a component opposes, and so reduces, the flow of current. It is measured in ohms.

questions.question: The diagram shows the structure of a corrugated card board. Which of the following reasons supports why it is commonly used for packaging?
questions.explanation: The fluted medium between the two liners traps air and acts like a cushion, so corrugated board absorbs knocks and protects the goods inside while staying light.

questions.question: Marking out on metal requires the identification of a
questions.explanation: On metal, all measurements are taken from a straight, filed reference edge called the datum edge. Face side and face edge are the reference surfaces used on wood.

questions.question: The diagram shows a method used to join metal pieces. What is the name of the method shown?
questions.explanation: The metal pieces are heated with a torch and a filler rod with a lower melting point is melted into the joint without melting the pieces themselves. Using a brass filler rod and a torch like this is brazing.

questions.question: Which of the following bits works on all woods and steel while offering greater longevity and durability?
questions.explanation: D is a high-speed steel twist bit. It drills both wood and metal and keeps its edge for a long time. A is a countersink, B an auger bit and C a Forstner-type bit, which are for wood only.

questions.question: Which of the following is a definition for a target market?
options: Consumers for a product or service
Most appealing features to the target
Media that the target turn to for information
questions.explanation: The target market is the group of customers a product or service is aimed at.

questions.question: The diagram shows pictorial drawings of electronic components. Which of the following components converts solar to electrical energy?
questions.explanation: W is the solar panel, which turns sunlight into electricity. X is the battery that stores it, Z the charge controller and Y the lamp.

questions.question: What is the voltage across the circuit shown below?
questions.explanation: Using V = I × R: 2 A × 12 Ω = 24 V. Voltage is measured in volts, so the answers in ohms cannot be right.

questions.question: Driver pulley A has a diameter of 100 mm and rotates at 300 rotations per minute (RPM). It is connected to driven pulley B, of diameter 500 mm. What is the rotation per minute of pulley B?
questions.explanation: Speed of B = speed of A × (diameter of A ÷ diameter of B) = 300 × 100 ÷ 500 = 60 RPM.

questions.question: Driver pulley A has a diameter of 100 mm and rotates at 300 rotations per minute (RPM). It is connected to driven pulley B, of diameter 500 mm. Which of the following statements is true about the mechanism?
options: Pulley B turns faster than pulley A.
Pulley A turns faster than pulley B.
Pulley A and pulley B turn at the same speed.
Pulley B and pulley A turn in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: The smaller pulley always turns faster: A turns at 300 RPM and B at 60 RPM. An open belt makes both pulleys turn in the same direction.

questions.question: Use the method of construction shown below. Which of the following statements is true?
options: Line MP is parallel to line NP.
Angle PMQ and angle PNQ are equal.
Angle MPO and angle NPO are supplementary.
questions.explanation: MPNQ has four equal sides, so it is a rhombus, and the opposite angles of a rhombus are equal: angle PMQ equals angle PNQ. PQ bisects MN, not NQ, MP meets NP at P, and angles MPO and NPO are equal, not supplementary.
